project_dependencies.use: PG766 already owns the inner thief designation; only the new simile is registered.
Inherited perfect-entitlement question retains the 45 earlier requests.

source_observations.observation: Instrumental support and comparison of conduct. Mere comparison of build, colour or ownership fails this guard.
Shows four different relations linking a nominal to the compared activity, cites the thief simile, and separately illustrates genitive and worthiness readings.
Pūrvavat includes the same cause of the earlier ātmanepada assignment. The text explicitly refuses transfer where that specific cause is missing.
The surface aikāgārikavad bhūmau compares conduct to that of a thief. It is a separate indeclinable use of PG766’s base.
Locative and genitive comparison. A place or owner supplies the comparison without being the compared article.
Accusative argument of worthiness. The king example shares a spelling with action comparison.
Vedic preverb conveying a verbal meaning with its participant. The Kāśikā section says 118 while the site's sūtra and Nyāsa headings say 117.
Agni goes to the high and low growths. Sāyaṇa supplies tall trees and low shrubs as accusative referents. Pada separates the preverbs.
A second Agni verse. The commentator explains the objects as high and low regions. Same two accusatives, different referents.
Locatives of the elevations and depressions in the grass and water passage. The commentator explicitly cites the preverb-vati rule.
The independent lexical annotations treat both landform nouns as feminine plural locatives.
Three preverb words are parallel with yāḥ and nadyaḥ. Sāyaṇa interprets them as the rivers which go in each direction or region.
